question.text:
Francesca uses 100 grams of lemon juice, 100 grams of sugar, and 400 grams of water to make lemonade. There are 25 calories in 100 grams of lemon juice and 386 calories in 100 grams of sugar. Water contains no calories. How many calories are in 200 grams of her lemonade?
  1. 129
  2. 137
  3. 174
  4. 233

Out of the following $4$ sentences, select the most suitable sentence with respect to grammar and usage:

  1. Since the report lacked needed information, it was of no use to them.
  2. The report was useless to them because there were no needed information in it.
  3. Since the report did not contain the needed information, it was not real useful to them.
  4. Since the report lacked needed information, it would not had been useful to them.
The letter F shown below is rotated $90^{\circ}$ clockwise around the origin, then reflected in the $y$-axis, and then rotated a half turn around the origin. What is the final image?

Bernardo and Silvia play the following game. An integer between 0 and 999 inclusive is selected and given to Bernardo. Whenever Bernardo receives a number, he doubles it and passes the result to Silvia. Whenever Silvia receives a number, she adds 50 to it and passes the result to Bernardo. The winner is the last person who produces a number less than 1000 . Let $N$ be the smallest initial number that results in a win for Bernardo. What is the sum of the digits of $N$ ?
  1. 7
  2. 8
  3. 9
  4. 10

For $x>0$, for which range of values of $\alpha$ is the following inequality true?
\[
x \log _{e}(x) \geq x-\alpha
\]

  1. $\alpha \geq 1 / 2$
  2. $\alpha \geq 0$
  3. $\alpha \leq 2$
  4. $\alpha \geq 1$

Three generations of the Wen family are going to the movies, two from each generation. The two members of the youngest generation receive a $50 \%$ discount as children. The two members of the oldest generation receive a $25 \%$ discount as senior citizens. The two members of the middle generation receive no discount. Grandfather Wen, whose senior ticket costs $\$ 6.00$, is paying for everyone. How many dollars must he pay?
  1. 34
  2. 36
  3. 42
  4. 46

Johann has 64 fair coins. He flips all the coins. Any coin that lands on tails is tossed again. Coins that land on tails on the second toss are tossed a third time. What is the expected number of coins that are now heads?
  1. 32
  2. 40
  3. 48
  4. 56

The number $25^{64} \cdot 64^{25}$ is the square of a positive integer $N$. In decimal representation, the sum of the digits of $N$ is
  1. 7
  2. 14
  3. 21
  4. 28

After Rajendra Chola returned from his voyage to Indonesia, he ________ to visit the temple in Thanjavur.

  1. was wishing
  2. is wishing
  3. wished
  4. had wished

Two years ago Pete was three times as old as his cousin Claire. Two years before that, Pete was four times as old as Claire. In how many years will the ratio of their ages be $2: 1$ ?
  1. 2
  2. 4
  3. 5
  4. 6

Consider four sets of vectors $A, B, C$ and $D$ in 3 . Out of these sets of vectors, one set is linearly dependent in 3.
Identity this linearly dependent set.
  1. $A=\{[1,1,1],[1,1,0],[1,0,0]\}$
  2. $B=\{[1,0,0],[0,1,1],[1,0,1]\}$
  3. $C=\{\{1,1,3],[0,2,1],[0,0,0]\}$
  4. $D=\{[1,1,1],[0,1,1],[2,0,1]\}$

Consider the matrix $A \in \mathbb{R}^{3 \times 4}$ given by:
$$
A=\left(\begin{array}{cccc}
1 & 2 & 3 & a \\
1 & 0 & -1 & 0 \\
0 & 1 & 2 & b
\end{array}\right)
$$
Which of the following statements is/are true regarding the dimension of the leftnull space of $A$ ?
A. If $a=2 b$, then $\operatorname{dim}(\operatorname{left}\operatorname{null}(A))=1$
B. If $a \neq 2 b$, then $\operatorname{dim}(\operatorname{left}\operatorname{null}(A))=0$
C. If $a=2 b$, then $\operatorname{dim}(\operatorname{left}\operatorname{null}(A))=0$
D If $a \neq 2 b$, then $\operatorname{dim}(\operatorname{left}\operatorname{null}(A))=1$

Let $f(n)=\Omega(n), g(n)=O(n)$ and $h(n)=\Theta(n)$. Then $[f(n) . g(n)]+h(n)$ is:

  1. $\Omega(\mathrm{n})$
  2. $O(n)$
  3. $\theta(n)$
  4. None of these

Which of the following statements are TRUE regarding positive semi-definite and positive-definite matrices?

  1. The singular values of a positive semi-definite matrix are the same as its eigenvalues.
  2. If a matrix $A$ is positive semi-definite, then there exists a matrix $B$ such that $B^{T} B=A$.
  3. The covariance matrix of any distribution is positive semi-definite and invertible.
  4. If the Hessian of a function is positive semi-definite, then the function is convex.

Suppose the random variable $U$ has uniform distribution on $[0,1]$ and $X=-2 \log U$. The density of $X$ is

  1. $f(x)= \begin{cases} e^{- x} & \text { if } x>0 \\ 0 & \text { otherwise }\end{cases}$
  2. $f(x)= \begin{cases}2 e^{-2 x} & \text { if } x>0 \\ 0 & \text { otherwise }\end{cases}$
  3. $f(x)=\left\{\begin{array}{cl}\frac{1}{2}e^{-\frac{x}{2}} & \text { if } x>0 \\ 0 & \text { otherwise }\end{array}\right.$
  4. $f(x)=\left\{\begin{array}{cl}\frac{x}{2} & \text { if } x \in[0,2] \\ 0 & \text { otherwise }\end{array}\right.$

Consider a centered design matrix $X \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times d}$, where $n$ is the number of examples and $d$ is the dimension of the examples. The singular value decomposition (SVD) of $X$ is given by $X=U D V^{\top}$. Which of the following matrices provide the coordinates of the data after projecting onto the principal components? Select all that apply.
  1. $X V$
  2. $U D$
  3. $D V^{T}$
  4. $X U$

Two independent random variables X and Y are uniformly distributed in the interval $[-1,1]$.The probability that $\max [X, Y]$ is less than $\frac{1}{2}$ is

  1. $\dfrac{3}{4}$
     
  2. $\dfrac{9}{16}$

Assume we have access to data $\left\{\left(x_{i}, y_{i}\right)\right\}_{i=1}^{n}$, where $x_{i} \in \mathbb{R}^{d}$ and $y_{i} \in \mathbb{R}$. Assume that we also have access to weights $\left\{w_{i}\right\}_{i=1}^{n}, w_{i} \in \mathbb{R}$ and $w_{i}>0$, which gives the "importance" of each data point. Our goal is to solve the weighted least squares regression problem:
$$
\begin{gathered}
\widehat{\theta}=\underset{\theta \in \mathbb{R}^{d}}{\arg \min } \sum_{i=1}^{n} w_{i}\left(x_{i}^{\top} \theta-y_{i}\right)^{2} . \\
\text { Denote } X=\left[\begin{array}{c}
x_{1}^{\top} \\
\vdots \\
x_{n}^{\top}
\end{array}\right] \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times d}, Y=\left[\begin{array}{c}
y_{1} \\
\vdots \\
y_{n}
\end{array}\right] \in \mathbb{R}^{n}, \text { and } W=\left[\begin{array}{cccc}
w_{1} & 0 & \ldots & 0 \\
0 & w_{2} & \ldots & 0 \\
\vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\
0 & 0 & \ldots & w_{n}
\end{array}\right] \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n} .
\end{gathered}
$$
What is $\widehat{\theta}$ in terms of $X, Y$, and $W$ ? One Answer

  1.  $W\left(X^{\top} X\right)^{-1} X^{\top} Y$
  2.  $\left(X^{\top} X\right)^{-1} X^{\top} W Y$
  3.  $\left(X^{\top} W X\right)^{-1} X^{\top} Y$
  4. $\left(X^{\top} W X\right)^{-1} X^{\top} W Y$

Consider the scenario where we aim to design a stack with the following operations:

  • push(x): Add element $x$ to the stack.
  • pop(): Remove the top element from the stack.
  • getMinimum(): Retrieve the minimum value from the stack without removing it.

We have the option to utilize additional stack(s) to achieve the desired functionalities. Which of the following statements is true?

  1. A minimum of 2 extra stacks is required to implement all three functions (push, pop, and getMinimum) in $O(1)$ time complexity.
  2. A minimum of 1 extra stack is required to implement all three functions (push, pop, and getMinimum) in $O(1)$ time complexity.
  3. To implement all three functions (push, pop, and getMinimum) in $O(1)$ time complexity, at least one extra stack and one extra queue are needed.
  4. Regardless of the number of extra stacks used, it is not possible to implement the getMinimum() function in $\mathrm{O}(1)$ time complexity.

Consider two independent random variables $X$ and $Y$ with identical distributions.The variables $X$ and $Y$ take value 0,1 and 2 with probabilities $\frac{1}{2}, \frac{1}{4}$ and $\frac{1}{4}$ respectively. What is conditional probability $P(X+Y=2 \mid X-Y=0)$ ?

  1. 0
  2. $\dfrac{1}{16}$
     
  3. $\dfrac{1}{6}$
     
  4. 1

Consider a binary search tree whose labels are each one capital letter, and assume that a level-order traversal yields the sequence $\text{"GENIUS"}.$ What is the preorder traversal of this tree?

  1. $\text{GENIUS}$
  2. $\text{GNEUIS}$
  3. $\text{GUINES}$
  4. $\text{GIUSEN}$

You are taking a multiple-choice exam that has 4 answers for each question. You are a smart student, so in answering a question on this exam, the probability that you know the correct answer is $p$, and you always choose the correct answer when you know it. If you don't know the answer, you choose one (uniformly) at random. What is the probability that you knew the correct answer to a question, given that you answered it correctly?

  1. $\dfrac{p+\frac{1-p}{4}}{p}$
     
  2. $\dfrac{p}{1+p}$
     
  3. $\dfrac{p}{p+\frac{1-p}{4}}$
     
  4. $\dfrac{p}{\frac{p}{4}+1}$

$$P \Updownarrow Q=\;\sim P \wedge Q$$
Which of the following statement is equivalent to $P \rightarrow Q$

  1. $\sim P \Updownarrow Q$
  2. $\sim(P \Updownarrow Q)$
  3. $\sim(\sim P \Updownarrow Q)$
  4. $\sim(\sim P \Updownarrow \sim Q)$

  1. $x_{t+1} \leftarrow-x_{t}+\eta \cdot abla_{x} f\left(x_{t} ight)$.
  2. $x_{t+1} \leftarrow x_{t}-\eta \cdot abla_{x} f\left(x_{t} ight)$.
  3. $x_{t+1} \leftarrow-x_{t}-\eta \cdot abla_{x} f\left(x_{t} ight)$.

Suppose a directed graph has a path from vertex X to vertex Y , but no path from vertex Y to vertex $\mathrm{X}$ The relationship between the finish times for depth-first search is: 

  1. finish $(\mathrm{X})<$ finish $(\mathrm{Y})$
  2. finish $(\mathrm{X})>$ finish $(\mathrm{Y})$
  3. $\operatorname{finish}(X)=\operatorname{finish}(Y)$
  4. could be either A. or B.

A random variable $X$ has probability density function $f(x)$ as given below:
$$f(x)=\begin{cases}ax+b, & \text{for } 0< x< 1 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{cases}$$
If the expected value $E[X]=2 / 3$, then $P[X<0.5]$ is ___$\qquad$

Assume you have a set of independent observations from a normally distributed population: $2,5,7,4$. If the mean $(\mu)$ of the population is known to be 4 , calculate the Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE) of the variance $\left(\sigma^{2}\right)$.
  1. $\sigma^{2}=3.0$

  3. $\sigma^{2}=4.5$

Let flip(p) be a procedure which returns 1 with probability $p$ and 0 with probability $1-p$.
Each call to flip is independent.
Consider the two following functions:

iterativeF(n,p):
    tot = 0
    for i = i to n:
        tot = tot + flip(p)
    return tot
recursiveF(n,p):
    if n <= 1:
        return flip(p)
    return 2*recursiveF(n/2,p)


Suppose we're given some power of two $n=2^{k}$ for $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and a legal probability $p \in[0,1]$.

  1. Expected value of iterative$\mathrm{F}(n, p)$ is $n p$
  2. Expected value of iterative$\mathrm{F}(n, p)$ is $n^2 p$
  3. Expected value of recursive$\mathrm{F}(n, p)$ is $n p$
  4. Expected value of recursive$\mathrm{F}(n, p)$ is $2^{np}$

The order of a leaf node in a $\text{B tree}$ is the maximum number of (value, data record pointer) pairs it can hold. Given that the block size is $1 \mathrm{~K}$ bytes(i.e. 1024 bytes), data record pointer is $7$ bytes long, the value field is $9$ bytes long and a block pointer is $6$ bytes long, what is the order of the leaf node?

1. $\left\{\left.\left[\begin{array}{c}t \\ s \\ \sin t\end{array}\right] \right\rvert\, t, s \in \mathbb{R}\right\}$

4. $\left\{\left.\left[\begin{array}{c}t \\ t+s \\ s\end{array}\right] \right\rvert\, t, s \in \mathbb{R}\right\}$

  1. 3 and 4 only
  2. 4 only
  3. 1, 3 and 4 only
  4. All of them

Consider the following predicates:

  • $\operatorname{bird}(x): x$ is a bird.
  • $ ext{penguin}(x): x$ is a penguin.
  • $ ext{fly} (x): x$ can fly.

Consider the following sentence:

All birds except penguins' fly. (Note that Penguins may or may not fly)

  1. $ orall x.[(\operatorname{bird}(x) \wedge eg$ penguin $(x)) ightarrow \mathrm{fly}(x)]$
  2. $ orall x.[ eg \operatorname{bird}(x) \vee eg$ penguin $(x) \vee$ fly $(x)]$
  3. $ orall x. [ eg$ bird $(x) \vee$ penguin $(x) \vee$ fly $(x)]$

Given a dataset $\mathrm{D}=\left\{\left(x_{i}, y_{i}\right)\right\}, x_{i} \in R^{k}, y_{i} \in=\{-1,+1\}, 1 \leq i \leq N$.

Suppose we train a hard-margin linear SVM on $n>100$ data points in $R^{2}$, yielding a hyperplane with exactly 2 support vectors. If we add one more data point and retrain the classifier, what is the maximum possible number of support vectors for the new hyperplane (assuming the $n+1$ points are linearly separable)?
Choose the correct answer:-

  1. 2
  2. $n$
  3. 3
  4. $n+1$

In the quicksort algorithm, you want to ensure stability while pivoting around the rightmost item p. Which of the following partitioning strategies should be used?

  1. Partition such that the left side of the pivot contains elements $\leq p$, and the right side contains elements > p.
  2. Partition such that the left side of the pivot contains elements $< $p, and the right sde contains elements $\geq $p.

  3. Partition such that the left side of the pivot contains elements $<\mathrm{p}$, and the right side contains elements $>\mathrm{p}$.
  4. It is not possible to make Quicksort a stable sorting algorithm.

Which of the following is/are true about a convex function $f(x): \mathbb{R}^{d} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ ?
  1. $f(x)$ must be differentiable across its entire domain.
  2. $f(x)$ has a unique global minimum.
  3. $g(x)=-f(x)$ is also convex.
  4. If $f(x)$ is twice differentiable, then $z^{\top} \nabla^{2} f(x) z \geq 0$ for all $z \in \mathbb{R}^{d}$.

Which of the following is/are NOT a valid rule about functional dependencies (FD's) in the context of RDBMS model?
  1. Reversitivity: if "A $\rightarrow \mathrm{B}$ " then " $\mathrm{B} \rightarrow \mathrm{A}$ "
  2. Kindatransitivity: if "A $\rightarrow \mathrm{C}$ " and " $\mathrm{AB} \rightarrow \mathrm{C}$ " then " $\mathrm{B} \rightarrow \mathrm{C}$ "
  3. Pseudotransitivity: if "A $\rightarrow \mathrm{B}$ " and " $\mathrm{BC} \rightarrow \mathrm{D}$ " then " $\mathrm{AC} \rightarrow \mathrm{D}$ "
  4. Union on LHS: If " $A \rightarrow B$ " and and " $C \rightarrow B$ " then " $A C \rightarrow B$ "

  1. $E\left[(X-c)^{2}\right]=(\mu-c)^{2}+\sigma^{2}$
  2. $E\left[(X-c)^{2}\right]=(\mu-c)^{2}$
  3. $E\left[(X-c)^{2}\right]=(\mu-c)^{2}-\sigma^{2}$
  4. $E\left[(X-c)^{2}\right]=(\mu-c)^{2}+2 \sigma^{2}$

  1. $0.20$
     
  2. $0.25$
     
  3. $0.30$
     
  4. $0.33$

  2. B and E are conditionally independent given C .
  3. $\mathrm{A}$ and D are marginally independent.

Which of the following is/are TRUE related to schemas used in warehousing databases?
  1. In a star schema, the primary keys are stored in the fact table and the foreign keys are stored in the dimension table.
  2. Star schemas can help eliminate update errors by reducing duplication of data.
  3. There is only one fact table being used in a star schema.

Which of the following $\text{ER}$ diagram represents the given requirements

$\text{“Every professor teaches exactly one course”}$

In class, we showed that the expected squared error can be decomposed into several important terms:
$$
\mathbb{E}\left[\left(Y-f_{\hat{\theta}}(x)\right)^{2}\right]=\sigma^{2}+\left(h(x)-\mathbb{E}\left[f_{\hat{\theta}}(x)\right]\right)^{2}+\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\mathbb{E}\left[f_{\hat{\theta}}(x)\right]-f_{\hat{\theta}}(x)\right)^{2}\right] .
$$ For which of the following reasons are we taking an expectation? In other words, what are the sources of randomness that we are considering in the derivation of the bias-variance tradeoff?
  1. We chose arbitrary features when doing feature engineering.
  2. We drew random samples from some larger population when we built our training set.
  3. There is some noise in the underlying process that generates our observations $\mathbf{Y}$ from our features.
  4. Our x values could have had missing or erroneous data, e.g. participants misreading a question on a survey.

Let $\operatorname{nbs}(m)=$ the number of possible Bayes Network graph structures using $m$ attributes. (Note that two networks with the same structure but different probabilities in their tables do not count as different structures). Which of the following statements is true?

  1. $m \leq \operatorname{nbs}(m)<\frac{m(m-1)}{2}$
  2. $\frac{m(m-1)}{2} \leq \operatorname{nbs}(m)<2^{m}$
  3. $2^{m} \leq \operatorname{nbs}(m)<2^{\frac{m(m-1)}{2}}$
  4. $2^{\frac{m(m-1)}{2}} \leq \operatorname{nbs}(m)$

Consider two identically distributed zero-mean random variables $U$ and $V$. Let the cumulative distribution functions of $U$ and $2 V$ be $F(x)$ and $G(x)$ respectively. Then, for all values of $x$:

  1. $F(x)-G(x) \leq 0$
  2. $F(x)-G(x) \geq 0$
  3. $(F(x)-G(x)) \cdot x \leq 0$
  4. $(F(x)-G(x)) \cdot x \geq 0$

In a classification task, the output labels are divided into the following categories:

  • $5 \%$ of instances belong to Class 1
  • $25\%$ belong to Class 2
  • $60 \%$ belong to Class 3
  • $10 \%$ belong to Class 4

The accuracy score is calculated as:
$$
\text { Average accuracy }=\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{N} \text { equals }\left(y_{i}, \hat{y}_{i}\right)}{N}
$$
where equals $\left(y_{i}, \hat{y}_{i}\right):=1$ when $y_{i}$ (actual tag) equals $\hat{y}_{i}$ (predicted tag), and 0 otherwise.
If the model assigns random labels so that each label is equally probable, what would the average accuracy score be?
 

  1. 5$\%$
  2. 25$\%$
  3. 33.3$\%$
  4. 50$\%$

  1. -2

  1. If two matrices are similar, then they have the same determinant.
  2. If two matrices have the same characteristic polynomial, then they are similar.
